details: US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded substantial net outflows of $411.92 million on November 6, contributing to a two-day total withdrawal of approximately $842 million. BlackRock's IBIT experienced the largest single-fund outflow with $403 million, while Fidelity's FBTC was a rare exception with a net inflow of $42.82 million. This institutional capital flight coincides with a wider "risk-off" sentiment in traditional financial markets, particularly affecting technology stocks, suggesting investors are reducing exposure to speculative assets.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See $412M Outflows as Tech Stocks Retreat

details: The cryptocurrency market experienced a decline of over 3% as speculation intensified regarding a potential Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December. A robust US jobs report for October, which significantly surpassed forecasts with 165,000 non-farm payrolls and saw the unemployment rate drop to 4.1%, has pushed the probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase to nearly 79%. Historically, Bitcoin has shown a tendency to fall in the month following Fed rate hikes that occur after a pause in monetary tightening, indicating potential continued downward pressure on crypto prices.
title: Crypto Market Dips Amid Strong Jobs Report, Higher Fed Hike Bets

details: The outcome of the recent US midterm elections, which saw the Democratic Party gain control of both chambers of Congress, has introduced fresh regulatory uncertainty for the cryptocurrency market. Analysts suggest that this shift in political power could lead to increased oversight and potentially stricter regulations for crypto companies. The prospect of prominent crypto critics assuming key leadership roles in congressional committees has heightened investor apprehension about a more challenging regulatory landscape for digital assets.
title: Democratic Control of Congress Raises Crypto Regulatory Concerns
